title: Continuity orchestrator: prefetch pacing and GPU slab-defrag for mixed-turn workloads
creator: Marcus Holloway
description:
Problem: Our continuous batching scheduler performs poorly under workloads with highly skewed prompt/response lengths (short user prompts followed by very long model-generated continuations). We observe KV cache fragmentation and GPU slab memory blowups during peak periods which increases p95 latency and causes occasional OOMs on older GPU SKUs.

Goal: Implement a 'continuity orchestrator' layer that coordinates prefetch pacing and lightweight slab-defrag heuristics to: 1) lower p95/p99 token latency for mixed-turn workloads, 2) reduce KV cache fragmentation and long-lived slab occupancy, and 3) maintain throughput (tokens/sec) within current SLA bounds. This work should be safe to roll out progressively and have clear roll-back and monitoring hooks.
acceptance_criteria: p95 token latency for mixed-turn synthetic benchmark decreases by >= 10% without reducing median throughput
No regression in tail latencies (>99th) on steady-state throughput for standard workloads
KV cache fragmentation score (as measured by kv_residency_skew metric) reduces by >= 20% in benchmark emulation of skewed dialogues
End-to-end canary rollout with gradual traffic shift and automatic fallback in 2 minutes if OOM or p99 spike detected
Unit/integration tests for orchestrator policy and deterministic sim harness added
Documentation for config knobs, telemetry events, and operator runbook added to Confluence
implementation_notes:
Design summary: Add a lightweight continuity orchestrator sitting between request admission and the continuous-batcher. It will: (A) maintain short-lived 'continuity sessions' for streams where generation is expected to be long, (B) assign a prefetch pacing budget per session that inflates KV pre-warm windows for predicted long-turns while throttling prefetch for short-turns, and (C) periodically trigger non-blocking slab-defrag passes when per-GPU free-fragment ratio crosses a threshold.

Key heuristics and interfaces:
- Continuity session detection: use a simple predictive model (length_prior = EWMA of historical response lengths per route) + explicit signal from model (response-estimate token count) when available.
- Prefetch pacing: budget is (estimated_response_tokens / pacing_factor). Requests that exceed budget are split into a 'foreground' immediate prefetch and a 'backfill' low-priority prefetch queued to best-effort pool.
- Slab defrag: implement a slow, cooperative compaction that reclaims cold KV segments by remapping low-use slabs onto contiguous pages; limit to one GPU slab thread per host and fail-open if compaction latency would affect SLO.
- Safety: orchestrator must not hold locks needed by the runtime during compaction; use epoch counters and copy-on-write remap.

Telemetry and knobs:
- New metrics: continuity.session_started, continuity.prefetch_budget, kv.slab_fragmentation_ratio, kv.segment_reclaimed, continuity.defrag_duration.
- Runtime knobs (configurable per-cluster): continuity.enabled, pacing_factor (float), defrag_threshold (percent), defrag_max_ms, backfill_queue_size.

Testing plan:
- Deterministic sim harness: extend the existing mixed-turn emulator to produce ground-truth for fragmentation and latency over 24-hour traces.
- Microbench: run canary on a small shard of dedicated GPUs (dev lab) with synthetic dialogs skewed 90% short prompts + 10% long completions.
- Gradual production rollout: start disabled, then phased enable for low-traffic routes, then per-region staggered ramp with automated rollback on OOM or >20% p95 regression.
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Spike completed; validated prefetch pacing idea on local sim. Preliminary results: pacing_factor=2 reduced peak KV occupancy by ~18% but increased average cold misses by 3%.
2026-03-04: Implemented continuity session API and integrated estimator hook into admission path. Added unit tests for session lifecycle.
2026-03-07: Implemented backfill queue and best-effort prefetch worker. Observed stable throughput in microbench but higher tail during defrag (next work item).
2026-03-09: Added prototype slab-defragmer with cooperative remap; initial run shows a 22% reduction in fragmentation metric but added a 30ms median pause in worst case—need to bound defrag window.
2026-03-10: Tuned defrag_max_ms to 15ms and introduced progressive chunking; re-ran benchmarks: fragmentation improvement persists (~19%) with median pause reduced to 6ms. Preparing canary PR.
review_comments: Priya (PM): Please include customer scenarios and mention which enterprise customers have reported related tail issues — link their tickets in Confluence.
Luis (Runtime): Concerned about copy-on-write overhead on older GPUs; suggests adding a fallback to mark segments read-only instead of remapping when memory bandwidth is saturated.
Ava (SRE): Add detailed alerting thresholds for kv.segment_reclaimed and continuity.defrag_duration. Also request circuit-breaker to prevent repeated defrag churn.
Design: Request mockups for operator console knobs and a simple Viz for slab fragmentation over time (Console needs to display per-GPU heatmap)
